recommended.why: Already read. Two of five filings active — the floor for "operational": at least one live registration.
The other half of that picture. Without it, "two are active" leaves three unaccounted for and the assessment cannot say whether the rest lapsed.
Two filings return no status at all. Reading it stops silence being mistaken for inactive.
Active specifically in the state of the submitted address — the registration that matters most for where the business says it operates.
Good standing is a question about the formation state, so the domestic filing's status is the one to read first.
Already read. This is the good-standing answer itself, and here it is a no_result — Delaware publishes no sub-status, so the honest answer is that it cannot be established from the record.
Whether the entity type agrees across all five registrations. A company operating under a type that disagrees with its filings is an identity problem, not an activity one.
"Operational" beyond the filings. A reachable site is evidence of trading that a registration cannot give you.
Corroboration of operating that does not depend on the company's own site being up.
Confirms nothing prohibited is being operated — relevant if "operational" is being asked as a gating question rather than a factual one.
